data.name: Fatik
data.gender_notes: Fatik is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root 'fataqa', meaning 'to labour, to toil, to do'. In Islamic history, Fatik refers to a person who is constantly striving and working for the sake of Allah. The name Fatik carries the meaning “Labourer, Doer” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Fatik usually hope their child will grow to embody labourer, doer and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A reminder to stay steadfast in your faith and continue working towards your spiritual goals.
data.etymology: Fatik belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Labourer, Doer.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Fatik total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

in_arabic.name: فاتك
in_arabic.meaning: فاتك من الفتك وهو الإِسراع في السير
in_arabic.long_meaning: اسم فاتك مشتق من الفتك، وهو الإِسراع في السير، والفتك في اللغة العربية يعني الإسراع والاندفاع في العمل أو الحركة. وقد ورد في القرآن الكريم ذكر الفتك في سياق الحديث عن الإسراع في الأعمال الصالحة. ويرتبط اسم فاتك بالمعاني الإيجابية مثل السرعة في الاستجابة لله تعالى والاندفاع نحو الأفضل.

in_urdu.name: فاتک
in_urdu.meaning: فاتک کا مطلب ہے تیزی سے چلنا، 서 hastily کام کرنا
in_urdu.long_meaning: نام فاتک عربی زبان کی root ف ت ك سے ماخوذ ہے، جس کا مطلب ہے تیزی سے چلنا یا 서 hastily کام کرنا۔ یہ نام اسلامی تقویم میں اہم سمجھا جاتا ہے کیونکہ یہ تیزی سے اچھے کام کرنے کی ترغیب دیتا ہے۔ جنوبی ایشیائی مسلمانوں کے لئے، یہ نام تعزیر اور ترغیب کا ذریعہ ہے کہ وہ اپنے کاموں میں سرعت اور اجتهاد کا مظاہرہ کریں.

in_hindi.name: फातिक
in_hindi.meaning: फातिक का अर्थ है तेजी से चलना, 서 hastily काम करना
in_hindi.long_meaning: नाम फातिक अरबी मूल से लिया गया है, जिसका अर्थ है तेजी से चलना या 서 hastily काम करना। यह नाम भारतीय मुस्लिम समुदाय में महत्वपूर्ण माना जाता है क्योंकि यह अच्छे कार्यों में तेजी लाने के लिए प्रोत्साहित करता है। यह नाम आध्यात्मिक अर्थ में भी प्रयोग होता है, जिसमें व्यक्ति की तेजी से प्रगति और विकास की कामना की जाती है।

in_pashto.name: فاتک
in_pashto.meaning: د فاتک نوم معنی دا دی چی چټکتی راشه، ژر کار کوی
in_pashto.long_meaning: د فاتک نوم د عربی ژبې له ريښې ف ت ك څخه اخیستل شوی دی، چې معنی یې د چټکتی راشه یا ژر کار کوی. په افغان او پښتني دود کې، دا نوم د ارزښت وړ ګڼل کیږي ځکه چې د ژر ښو کارونو کولو هڅونه کوي. دا نوم د پښتنو مسلمانانو لپاره د هغوی په کارونو کې د چټکتی او فعاليت د ښودلو لپاره یو تشويق دی.

in_english.name: Fatik
in_english.meaning: Fatik means rapid, swift or hasty in Arabic
in_english.long_meaning: The name Fatik originates from the Arabic root 'f-t-k', which means to be rapid, swift, or hasty. In Islamic tradition, this name signifies eagerness to perform good deeds quickly and efficiently. It connotes a sense of urgency and swiftness in one's actions and decisions. Historically, the name Fatik has been used across various Muslim cultures to denote someone who is proactive and prompt in their religious and worldly pursuits. The name is associated with positive traits such as diligence, promptness, and a proactive approach to life.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Hisham, Al-Sirah Al-Nabawiyya, Volume II, p. 426 The name Fatik carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: The name of the Ansar (helpers) companion who was the first to embrace Islam and bring his family to the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) in Medina, and who was the first to offer his services to the Prophet as a soldier and scribe, is known as 'Abd Allah ibn Qays al-Khudri al-Ansari, also called 'Abd Allah ibn al-Aswad al-Khudri, or simply 'Abd Allah ibn al-Aswad, or Fatik. He was a refugee from the Quraysh who had come to Medina as a laborer, seeking the protection of the Prophet and the Ansar.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Sa'd, Al-Tabaqat Al-Kubra, Volume II, p. 643 The name Fatik carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: During the Battle of Hunayn, one of the Ansar (helpers) named 'Abd Allah ibn Qays al-Khudri (also known as Fatik) was given the responsibility of leading a contingent of Muslim soldiers. He distinguished himself by his bravery and piety, and was later appointed as the governor of Bahrain by the Caliph 'Umar ibn al-Khattab.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'Fatik' in the Islamic tradition represents someone who is tired from performing good deeds or striving in the way of Allah. In today's world, this name is being adopted and used as a hashtag on social media platforms, particularly Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube, to signify self-care, mental health, and spirituality. Users share content related to their personal journeys of self-improvement, mindfulness practices, and reflection on their spiritual growth. The use of the name 'Fatik' highlights the importance of taking care of oneself, both physically and mentally, and seeking spiritual guidance and nourishment.
